newsitem.title: SYRIA: Syria's assad receives U.S. message.
newsitem.headline: Syria's assad receives U.S. message.

text.p: The U.S. ambassador on Friday delivered a letter from U.S. President Bill Clinton to Syrian President Hafez al-Assad.
Presidential spokesman Joubran Kourieh said Assad gave U.S. ambassador Christopher Ross a reply but revealed no details of either letter.

Clinton's message came a day after Assad discussed with Lebanese Foreign Minister Faris Bouez threats that Israel might launch a major attack against Lebanon and reports of Syrian troops redeployments in Lebanon.
It also followed Washington's announcement that Israel and the United States, sponsor of Middle East peace talks, had new proposals to restart Syrian-Israeli negotiations.
Witnesses said on Thursday that Syria, the main foreign power broker in Lebanon with 35,000 troops, had redeployed troops in Beirut and other parts of the country.
Bouez said threats by Israel's ally General Antoine Lahd, commander of the South Lebanese Army, were aimed at forcing Lebanon to accept Israeli peace proposals.
